children: CONSUMER STOCKS PUSH STOXX CLOSE TO AUGUST PEAK

European shares extended their post-midterm rally on Thursday, as a rebound in consumer stocks after months of pressure from high energy costs helped lift the STOXX 600 to within striking distance of its August record high.
gained 0.6%, also supported by gains in materials, autos, banks, real estate and software as investors kept rotating out of chip stocks that have led much of the global bull market in recent years.

Oil and gas (.SXEP) led decliners, falling over 1% to a one-month low, while travel and leisure (.SXTP) hit a record high, as airlines rallied on bets that easing tensions in the Middle East could lower fuel costs and support travel demand.
Luxury (.STXLUXP), another sector sensitive to tourism flows and consumer confidence, were also among the strongest gainers, rising 2%. Brent prices
firmed just above $95, but remained on track for their biggest weekly drop since 2020.
rose 1% to a record high, while the FTSE 100
touched a three-month peak ahead of an expected Bank of England interest-rate hike later in the day, which would be its first in three years.
